label: SEM Lab specification — not extracted from the SmartPLS project file
summary: ACSI base model without the complaints construct, matching the 'ACSI (modified)' / 'ACSI (without COMP)' naming of the sample files and the five constructs present in the measurement assignment.
measurementMode: reflective (SEM Lab's choice; the plain side files do not state the measurement mode)

variants.summary: Full base model of Fig. 1 with complaints as a single-indicator construct COMPL measured by the binary item COMP: adds CUSA -> COMPL and COMPL -> CUSL. Needs an explicit decision on how a binary single indicator is treated; not recommended as a default example.

citations: Fornell, C., Johnson, M. D., Anderson, E. W., Cha, J., & Bryant, B. E. (1996). The American Customer Satisfaction Index: Nature, purpose, and findings. Journal of Marketing, 60(4), 7-18. https://doi.org/10.1177/002224299606000403

Morgeson, F. V., III, Hult, G. T. M., Sharma, U., & Fornell, C. (2023). The American Customer Satisfaction Index (ACSI): A sample dataset and description. Data in Brief, 48, 109123. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2023.109123
citationBasis: All nine arrows of the base model were read from Fig. 1 ('The ACSI base model') of Morgeson et al. (2023), which was opened; the seven proposed paths are the seven that do not involve complaints. Fornell et al. (1996) is cited as the original model and was not opened.
notes: CUSL is measured by the single indicator REPUR: reliability and AVE are not applicable; in CB-SEM the error variance of a single indicator must be fixed.

HIGHPTOL and LOWPTOL (price tolerance) are in the data but are not assigned to CUSL in the sample. They contain the codes 26 and 101 although the data dictionary gives 0-25 as the valid range; do not use them as indicators without a documented recode.
COMP is binary (0/1) and HANDLE is answered only by complainers (1,371 of 8,239).
Missing data: the 12 model indicators have missing values, so this dataset is the natural listwise-versus-FIML fixture. The sample's own setting for missing values is MEAN_REPLACEMENT.
